key_insight: Deep learning predicted HPV/p16 status from routine vulvar cancer slides more accurately than it distinguished all three molecular subtypes.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support HPV-stratified retrospective outcome research without consuming additional tissue; it is not a validated replacement for ancillary testing.
method: Extracted features from routine H&E whole-slide images using H-optimus-1.
Trained attention-based models: HERA for HPV/p16 status and HERMES for three molecular subtypes.
Developed models on 644 patients and tested them on 286 patients from two independent cohorts.
evidence_signal: Independent testing yielded an AUC of 0.84 for HERA and a macro-average AUC of 0.70 for HERMES; predicted groups also showed prognostic separation.
watch_item: Broader external validation of discrimination and calibration across scanners and populations is needed, particularly given limited separation of HPV-independent subtypes.
paper_title: Predicting HPV/p16 Status and Molecular Subtypes from Histopathology Slides using Deep Learning in Vulvar Squamous Cell Carcinoma
